name: integrated-browser-mcp
description: Exposes VS Code's integrated browser to external agents (Claude Code, scripts, curl) via a local HTTP API and MCP server.

enumDescriptions: Prefer a unix socket / named pipe; fall back to a TCP port if one cannot be created
Require a unix socket / named pipe; fail startup rather than open a port
Always listen on a TCP port (needed only when the MCP client cannot reach this machine's filesystem)
integratedBrowserMcp.transport.description: How external agents reach the bridge. The default avoids opening any listening port: it binds a unix socket (or named pipe on Windows) that no other machine can reach and no port scan can find. TCP remains available for setups where the MCP client and the extension host do not share a filesystem.

integratedBrowserMcp.httpPort.description: TCP port used only when integratedBrowserMcp.transport resolves to tcp. Ignored when listening on a socket/pipe.

integratedBrowserMcp.autoStart.description: Automatically start the bridge when VS Code opens

enumDescriptions: Prefix '(N) ' — lets you say "reload browser 2" and match browser_tab_list's number
Prefix a fixed symbol — shows the tab is agent-controlled without implying an ordering
integratedBrowserMcp.tabIndicator.description: How to mark browser tabs that are under agent control. Only tabs the bridge opened itself are marked — pages you opened are never touched. Marking works by rewriting the page's real document.title (the only lever an extension has over the editor tab label), so the page can observe it: choose 'off' if a page or tool needs the unmodified title, e.g. when reading it back via browser_eval.

enumDescriptions: Black circle — widest font coverage, renders essentially everywhere
Black diamond — geometric, also very widely supported
High voltage — colour emoji; needs an emoji font (absent on bare Linux)
Robot — colour emoji, unambiguously 'an agent'; same font caveat
Plain ASCII — cannot fail to render, at the cost of width
integratedBrowserMcp.tabIndicatorText.description: Symbol shown on tabs the agent controls when integratedBrowserMcp.tabIndicator is 'marker'. A trailing space is added automatically. Emoji options render in colour on Windows and macOS but can appear as a placeholder box on systems without an emoji font.

integratedBrowserMcp.enforceSharing.description: Restrict the bridge to tabs it opened itself. When on, tabs you opened (which the bridge otherwise adopts and can drive) are detached, and later calls on their tabId fail; browser_tab_open / browser_navigate still create bridge-owned tabs, so agents keep working. Works on every VS Code build. Off by default: without it, the bridge drives every browser tab in the window and VS Code's share/unshare does not affect it.

enumDescriptions: VS Code integrated browser (runs inside VS Code)
External Chrome window (more reliable CDP support)
integratedBrowserMcp.browserType.description: Which browser type to launch for automation

languageModelTools.name: integratedBrowser_console
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read buffered console output from the integrated browser
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read buffered console output (log/warn/error) captured from integrated browser pages, including messages from web workers and iframes. The buffer is continuous — it contains messages emitted before this call, which a screenshot or page read cannot recover. Use for diagnosing runtime errors.

tabId.description: Optional bridge tab id. Omit to aggregate across all tabs.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (newest last). Default 50, max 200.

languageModelTools.name: integratedBrowser_network
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read buffered network requests from the integrated browser
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read buffered network requests/responses (method, url, status, type, timing) captured from integrated browser pages. The buffer is continuous, so it includes requests already completed before this call. Use to check failing API calls, status codes, or whether a request fired at all.

tabId.description: Optional bridge tab id. Omit to aggregate across all tabs.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (newest last). Default 50, max 200.

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the request URL.

languageModelTools.name: integratedBrowser_downloads
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read download events from the integrated browser
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read buffered download events (guid, url, suggested filename, state, bytes, resolved path) from integrated browser pages. Use to confirm a download started, completed, or where the file landed.

tabId.description: Optional bridge tab id. Omit to aggregate across all tabs.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (newest last). Default 50, max 200.

languageModelTools.name: integratedBrowser_tabs
languageModelTools.userDescription: List integrated browser tabs the bridge is driving
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the integrated browser tabs this bridge is attached to: tabId, number, url, title, icon, active flag, connection state and transport. Complements the built-in browser tools by showing what the bridge itself can drive.
